Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

manage verb

succeed in doing

also manage to, succeed in, can you manage?, if you can manage it

classical

Catull. 76.14: vērum hoc quā lubet efficiās

efficiō, efficere, effēcī, effectum

verb, third conjugation (-iō); with an accusative, or ut and the subjunctive

manage, bring it about (that)

Lewis & Short: “to bring to pass, to effect, execute, complete, accomplish”. Often Latin needs no verb for “manage”: the plain verb with tandem, vix or aegrē says it (vix aperuī, I only just managed to open it).

Other words

  • cōnficiō, cōnficere, cōnfēcī, cōnfectum — get (something) done

    verb, third conjugation (-iō), transitive · also used · classical · Traupman 343: sī id cōnficere poteris, if you can manage it

    See complete.

  • contingit (mihi) ut — I get to, I have the chance to (by good fortune)

    verb, impersonal; with the dative, and ut or an infinitive · also used · classical · Quint. 1.1.7: quibus discere ipsīs nōn contigit; Tac. Agr. 45.4: nōn contigit

    Of what falls to one’s lot, not of effort.

Examples

  • difficile est longum subitō dēpōnere amōrem, difficile est, vērum hoc quā lubet efficiās

    It is hard to lay down a long love all at once; it is hard, but you must manage it somehow.Catull. 76.13–14

  • nec tamen iī, quibus discere ipsīs nōn contigit, minōrem cūram docendī līberōs habeant

    Yet parents who never had the chance to learn should take no less care over teaching their children.Quint. 1.1.7

  • Tandem aperuī!

    I managed to open it at last!composed

  • Sī id cōnficere poteris …

    If you can manage it …Traupman 343

See also achieve, try, manage, complete.
